review_note: REJECTED. Seed G0102 (Wizard Spider) is correctly found and is the only doc that satisfies financially-motivated + ransomware + healthcare. Two disqualifiers: (1) under-specified pivot let bm25-only lexical distractors in as rel=1, including state actors that contradict the query (G0088 TEMP.Veles = TRITON state actor, not financial/ransomware; G1027 CyberAv3ngers = IRGC PLC actor) plus FIN7/GOLD SOUTHFIELD/REvil distractors. (2) Second hop is ungrounded: Wizard Spider/TrickBot/Ryuk have no ATT&CK-for-ICS mapping (IT actor), so the T-/M-codes are judge speculation, not documented ground truth. Cannot salvage by pruning to G0102 — the ICS-mitigation clause has no clean answer set. Consider re-drafting to name a discriminator and drop the false ATT&CK-for-ICS premise.

review_note: ACCEPTED after relabel. Query is sound and answerable; pool was inflated with ~30 CISA advisories via lexical DoS/I/O/packet overlap. Relabeled 29 docs (see relabel_log): promoted NIST 5 (Architecture) + 5.1.2 (Defense-in-Depth) and seed + ICSA-23-236-06 to rel=2; demoted 24 CISA advisories to 0 (17 wrong-component: PLCs/relays/servers/software not discrete I/O modules; 7 wrong-vuln-class: DLL/permissions, code injection, deserialization, privilege, side-channel info-leak) plus nist:0 Executive Summary. review_note: ACCEPTED after relabel. text: What are the main exploitation techniques that should be detected and blocked as part of a comprehensive exploit protection strategy in industrial control systems?
note: An OT security practitioner would naturally ask this question when designing detection and prevention controls for their ICS environment. They need to understand which exploitation vectors their exploit protection capabilities should address, without necessarily knowing the specific MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs. This question is answerable directly from the document, which lists the five key exploitation techniques that exploit protection mitigates: evasion exploits, privilege escalation exploits, remote service exploitation, public-facing application exploitation, and drive-by compromise attacks.
review_note: REJECTED - under-specified query (seed leakage). Read on its own terms, "main exploitation techniques ... comprehensive exploit protection strategy in ICS" has no stable answer set: it could mean any T0xxx exploitation technique, the Initial Access/Execution tactic sets, NIST vulnerability-management guidance, or M0950's particular five. "Main" is undefined and "comprehensive strategy" signals breadth. The query's apparent match to M0950 is an artifact of being generated FROM M0950, not retrievable precision. Empirical confirmation: the pool is diffuse (30 docs flat at rel=1 spanning NIST strategy chapters, 21 CISA advisories with 0/21 exploit-protection signal, and unrelated MITRE docs M0931/T1691.002/T1692.002) - three independent retrievers did not converge, the signature of a vague query. Structural cause: M0950 is a 350-char cross-reference stub whose only content is its "Addresses techniques" pointer list, so the "do not name document identifiers" drafting constraint admits no valid natural question. Contrast q001/q004: similarly thin seeds but with distinctive proper nouns (CSET, ICSJWG) to anchor the question. qrels left as judged - not relabeled. Also noted: 4 of M0950's 5 named techniques (T0890, T0866, T0819, T0817) exist in the corpus but were never pooled - a genuine coverage gap.

review_note: ACCEPTED after relabel. Query is sound: tight discriminators (Siemens industrial switches + telnet + remote DoS) and both halves have real substrate. Judge drafted 25 relevant of 36; relabeled 13. Key fix: the SEED cisa:ICSA-19-225-03 (SCALANCE X Switches) was UNDER-graded at rel=1 despite being the unique doc carrying telnet+DoS+switch+SCALANCE - promoted to 2, since a retriever finding it was scoring below one finding the generic architecture chapter. Promoted nist:257 (F.7.1 ACCESS CONTROL - AC, 70 AC- refs) to 2 as the direct answer to the NIST-alignment half. Demoted 11 to 0: nist:276 (Appendix G Change Log - a 726-char revision changelog), nist:0 (exec summary), nist:253/4.3.3/4.3.7/5.4.3 (generic, zero signal), nist:263 (F.7.7 IA - wrong control family; query asks access control = AC), and 4 advisories (3 Hitachi vendor-boilerplate cluster + Siemens Industrial Edge Management, which is software not a switch and has no telnet vector). Kept nist:273 (F.7.17 SC, holds SC-5 Denial of Service Protection) at 1 - real but it is the threat control, not the segmentation/access-control asked for. Final: 4 rel=2 + 10 rel=1. This query also exposed a calibration gap in scan_suspect_labels.py (DOMAIN_STOP lacked query-scaffolding words, letting the Hitachi cluster bank free matches on access/controls/should); DOMAIN_STOP has since been widened.
